text: premiums are a waste, I'd rather keep the money in savings
I can skip a personal health policy and keep the money I would spend on premiums in savings.

chain.why: A single private‑hospital stay can cost about ₹24,000, which can exceed the amount saved by skipping premiums.
About 1 in 9 Indian adults aged 20 and over has diabetes, and more than 1 in 3 has high blood pressure.
A fresh policy bought after leaving a job, rather than migrated, starts its waiting periods from zero.
Of about 3.7 crore health claims handled in 2024–25, 87% were paid, 8% were rejected and about 5% were still pending at year end.

conclusion: Since a private‑hospital stay can cost ₹24,000, many adults already have diabetes or hypertension, a new policy would start waiting periods from zero, and most health claims are paid, skipping personal coverage risks large out‑of‑pocket expenses.

text: I hear you want to keep your money in savings. According to MoSPI/NSO, NSS 80th round press note, 20 Apr 2026, the typical private‑hospital stay costs about ₹24,000 (≈$248) out of pocket. If you had to cover a stay like that, how would that compare to the amount you’d save by skipping premiums?
